leo: Noticed weirdness in node + go sampleapps: req_id present in traces but some logs show `<redacted>` only after a retry path. Could be OTEL hook ordering or our redact hook hitting before context is attached.

anya: Ugh. Which sampleapps and steps? I can try to repro quickly.

leo: node sample-app v0.3.1, go sample-auth v0.2. Steps:
1) set REDACT=on, LOG_LEVEL=info
2) start both apps locally with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318
3) call /signin that triggers token refresh (we simulate a 401 then 200)

Observed (node):
```
info auth: signin start user=bob req_id=xyz-001
debug http: token refresh attempt=1
info auth: signin success user=bob req_id=<redacted>
```
Trace span attributes: req_id=xyz-001 (OTLP shows full id)

Observed (go):
```
INFO auth/handler: start req_id=xyz-002
INFO retry/middleware: retrying
INFO auth/handler: success req_id=<redacted>
```

ben: Does the redactor look for the req_id string in the formatted log text or does it consult the active span attributes? If it's text-only, async exporter batching or racey span attach could cause this.

leo: From a quick read of the node-redact middleware it runs as a formatting hook before the otel emitter attaches span attrs. So racey ordering possible.

anya: Easy mitigation: ensure middleware attaches req_id to the request context and create the span with that attribute up front. Also add a safe ordering comment in quickstart for both runtimes.

ben: Longer term: make the redact hook inspect span attributes or pass a structured field to the formatter instead of doing regex over formatted msg. That avoids partial redact when log message emitted before span is enriched.

leo: I'll open a tiny PR for node sampleapp to attach req_id earlier and add a unit test that flips log level mid-flow. Also will plumb a note into the quickstart about ordering.

devops-bot: Created TICKET-5421: "sampleapps: make req_id propagation + redaction deterministic across retries" (https://redwood.internal/TICKET-5421)

anya: Thanks. If someone with go context can paste the minimal redaction middleware snippet we can do the same pattern there.

ben: Pasting go snippet (trimmed):
```
func Redact(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
  return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    reqID := r.Header.Get("X-Request-Id")
    ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), ReqIDKey, reqID)
    span := tracer.Start(ctx, "request", trace.WithAttributes(attribute.String("req_id", reqID)))
    defer span.End()
    next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(span.Context()))
  })
}
```
This pattern fixed it locally for me.

leo: Perfect, I'll mirror that in node and add a comment explaining why redaction must consult span attrs.

anya: Great. We'll also add an integration smoke test that toggles RETRY to force the 401->200 path so we don't regress.

ben: Sounds good.

leo: Filing a follow-up to check our hosted logs pipeline to ensure redaction plugin ordering is consistent across deploys.

anya: ping me on the PR, happy to review. :thumbsup:
